blocks.instruction: Read the passage and answer the questions. Write True or False for the true-false questions.

stimulus.text: The school was closed for the summer holidays. But the garden still needed water. So Mrs Rao, the class teacher, made a list. Two children came each morning with a bucket. The sun was hot, so they came early. On Monday, Meena and Zoya watered the roses. On Tuesday, Arjun and Kabir watered the tomato plants. On Wednesday, Farah and Dev cleaned the paths and watered the marigolds. They poured the water slowly near the roots. Mohan Kaka, the watchman, opened the gate for them every day. He also filled the buckets at the tap. On the last day, all the children came together. The roses were red and pink. The tomatoes were round and ripe. Mrs Rao gave each child one tomato to take home. Everyone was proud of the garden.

items.q: Why did the children come to the school during the holidays?
items.answer: To water the garden

items.q: How many children came each morning?
items.answer: Two

items.q: Who watered the tomato plants?
items.answer: Arjun and Kabir

items.q: What did Farah and Dev do on Wednesday?
items.answer: They cleaned the paths (1) and watered the marigolds (1).

items.q: What did Mrs Rao make at the start, and what did she give each child on the last day?
items.answer: She made a list (1). She gave each child one tomato to take home (1).

items.q: These jobs are in the wrong order. Write a, b and c in the order in which they were done. (a) Farah and Dev watered the marigolds. (b) Meena and Zoya watered the roses. (c) Arjun and Kabir watered the tomato plants.
items.answer: b, c, a. (b) roses on Monday, (c) tomato plants on Tuesday, (a) marigolds on Wednesday. Full order — 2; b first but c and a swapped — 1; b not first — 0.

answerPoints.point: c comes second and a comes third

items.q: The school was closed for the summer holidays.
items.answer: True. The first sentence says so.

items.q: Farah and Dev watered the roses.
items.answer: False. Meena and Zoya watered the roses; Farah and Dev watered the marigolds.

items.q: Which flowers did Farah and Dev water? Write one word from the passage.
items.answer: marigolds

items.q: On which day did Arjun and Kabir water the plants? Write one word.
items.answer: Tuesday

items.q: (a) Who made the list? (1 mark) (b) Write two ways in which Mohan Kaka helped the children. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Mrs Rao, the class teacher (1). (b) He opened the gate for them every day (1). He filled the buckets at the tap (1).

answerPoints.point: filled the buckets at the tap

blocks.instruction: Read the poem and answer the questions.

stimulus.text:
The sun sinks low, the sky is gold.
Four runners wait, so brave and bold.
Asha runs first and passes the stick.
Ravi takes it and runs so quick.
Then Meena takes it, her steps so light.
Sunil is last and holds it tight.
He crosses the line and hears the crowd.
Four friends hug and cheer out loud.

items.q: Write the names of the four runners in the order in which they run.
items.answer: Asha, Ravi, Meena, Sunil. All four in order — 2; Asha first and Sunil last but the middle two swapped — 1.

items.q: What time of day is the race? Write the words from the poem that tell you.
items.answer: It is evening (or sunset) (1). “The sun sinks low, the sky is gold.” (either half of the line) (1).

answerPoints.point: the sun sinks low / the sky is gold

items.q: What do the four friends do when the race ends?
items.answer: They hug (1) and cheer out loud (1).

items.q: The sun sinks low and the sky is _____.
items.answer: gold

items.q: Ravi takes the stick and runs so _____.
items.answer: quick

items.q: Meena’s steps are so _____.
items.answer: light

items.q: How many runners are in the team?
items.answer: Four

items.q: Who takes the stick after Ravi?
items.answer: Meena

items.q: (a) Who passes the stick to Ravi? (1 mark) (b) Write two things that Sunil does in the last part of the race. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Asha (1). (b) Any two: he holds the stick tight (1); he crosses the line (1); he hears the crowd (1).

answerPoints.point: first thing Sunil does (holds the stick tight / crosses the line / hears the crowd)

blocks.instruction: Answer the following questions. Use the poem “Together We Can” and the activities in your textbook to help you.

items.q: The poem says, “Helping each other, we never fall.” Give two reasons why helping each other is important for a team.
items.answer: Any two sensible reasons, 1 mark each. For example: the team stays strong and does not give up (1); the work is done faster (1); nobody feels alone (1).
items.markingGuide: One mark for each sensible reason, written in a sentence. Two reasons — 2; one reason — 1. Repeating the same reason twice earns 1. Maximum 2.
items.chapterSource: poem l.2; Let us Think A2

items.q: Look at lines 5 and 6 of the poem in your textbook. What does the team always do, win or lose? What is always there for the team?
items.answer: The team always shares (1). Their bond of trust is always there (1).

answerPoints.point: the bond of trust is always there

items.q: Look at lines 7 and 8 of the poem in your textbook. What two things happen when each hand is joined?
items.answer: The goal is near (1). Team spirit fills the air with cheer (1).

answerPoints.point: team spirit fills the air with cheer

items.chapterSource: poem l.7-8; Let us Think A1

items.q: Imagine that your team loses a game. Write two sentences: how you would feel, and what you would say to your team.
items.answer: Any sensible feeling in a full sentence (1); any kind or encouraging words to the team in a full sentence (1). For example: I would feel sad. I would say, “Well tried, we will do better next time.”

answerPoints.point: what you would say to the team

items.markingGuide: One mark for a sentence about feelings; one mark for a sentence of kind words to the team. Both — 2; one — 1. Maximum 2.

items.q: Honeybees and ants both work as a team. (a) How do honeybees tell their hive members where the flowers are? (b) Write one thing that ants do as a team using signals.
items.answer: (a) They do a waggle dance (1). (b) Any one: they find food, defend their colony, or build nests (1).

answerPoints.point: find food / defend their colony / build nests

items.q: Write five sentences on ONE of these. (a) Sameer sees a small girl drop her books in the corridor. He is picking them up for her. Write five sentences about what Sameer is doing now and what will happen next. OR (b) Write five sentences to tell a friend how to make the paper cut-out figure from the “Working Together” activity in your textbook. Use the words first, next, then, after that and last.
items.answer: Model for (a): Sameer is picking up the girl’s books. He is smiling at her. He is putting the books in her bag. The girl will say thank you. She will walk to her class with a happy face. Model for (b): First, fold a sheet of paper. Next, draw one side of a body along the fold. Then cut along the drawing. After that, unfold the paper gently. Last, colour the figure.
items.markingGuide: One mark for each sentence on the chosen topic that is complete and makes sense: five sentences — 5; four — 4; three — 3; two — 2; one — 1. For (a), at least two sentences must say what will happen next using will; if none uses will, deduct 1. For (b), the steps must be correct and in order. Deduct 1 for more than three spelling errors. Minimum 0.
items.chapterSource: Let us Write (what is happening, what will happen next); Let us Do A (Working Together)

blocks.instruction: Write a paragraph in your notebook.

items.q: Families in our country keep many festivals and cook many kinds of food. Write a paragraph of five or six sentences about a festival that your family enjoys. These lines will help you. 1. The festival my family enjoys most is … 2. To get ready, we … 3. The best food on the table is … 4. The people who come together are … 5. My favourite part is … because …
items.answer: Model: The festival my family enjoys most is Diwali. To get ready, we clean the house and make small lamps. The best food on the table is jalebi. My uncles, aunts and cousins come together at our house. My favourite part is lighting the lamps because the whole street looks bright.

answerPoints.point: says how the family gets ready
gives a favourite part with a reason

items.markingGuide: One mark for each of the five points, written in a full sentence: all five points — 5; four — 4; three — 3; two — 2; one — 1. Deduct 1 for more than three spelling errors or missing capital letters and full stops. Minimum 0.
items.chapterSource: Let us Speak (favourite food and festival)

blocks.instruction: Think about the situation and write your answer.

items.q: You are the leader of a group that is making a poster. Two of your teammates cannot agree on the colours. Write what you would do to bring your team together again. Write five sentences and give at least three things you would do.
items.answer: Model: I would ask each teammate to say what they want. I would listen to both of them without interrupting. Then I would ask them to take turns: one colour for the sky and one for the ground. I would say that the poster is for the whole team. In the end we would all colour it together.

answerPoints.point: the team works together at the end

items.markingGuide: Three or more different, sensible steps in full sentences and the team working together again — 5; three steps — 4; two steps — 3; one step — 2; only a wish with no action (for example, they should be friends) — 1. Deduct 1 for more than three spelling errors. Minimum 0.

blocks.instruction: Make a sentence with each word. Use will in sentences (iv) and (v).

items.q: (i) teamwork
items.answer: Model: We finished the project because of good teamwork.
items.markingGuide: One mark for a correct sentence that uses the word teamwork. No mark if the word is missing or the sentence does not make sense. Maximum 1.

items.q: (ii) bundle
items.answer: Model: Grandfather tied a bundle of sticks with a rope.
items.markingGuide: One mark for a correct sentence that uses the word bundle. No mark if the word is missing or the sentence does not make sense. Maximum 1.
items.chapterSource: Let us Learn A (bundle of sticks)

items.q: (iii) bouquet
items.answer: Model: Nisha gave the singer a bouquet of roses.
items.markingGuide: One mark for a correct sentence that uses the word bouquet. No mark if the word is missing or the sentence does not make sense. Maximum 1.

items.q: (iv) defend
items.answer: Model: The ants will defend their colony.
items.markingGuide: One mark for a correct sentence that uses the word defend and will. No mark if the word is missing or the sentence does not make sense. Maximum 1.
items.chapterSource: Know You Do (ants defend their colony)

items.q: (v) languages
items.answer: Model: We will learn many languages.
items.markingGuide: One mark for a correct sentence that uses the word languages and will. No mark if the word is missing or the sentence does not make sense. Maximum 1.
items.chapterSource: Let us Speak (languages); Let us Write (will)

blocks.instruction: Look at the map. Imagine that you stand at the road and look at the buildings. For 1 to 4, fill in the blanks with the words from the box. Use each word once. Box: behind, between, near, in front of. For 5 and 6, choose the correct word from the brackets.

stimulus.caption: A street map. It shows these places: bank, school, post office, hospital, bookstore and park. The road is called Main Road.

items.q: The school is _____ the park.
items.answer: in front of

items.q: The bank is _____ the post office and the school.
items.answer: between

items.q: The hospital is _____ the bank.
items.answer: behind

items.q: The post office is _____ the bank.
items.answer: near

items.q: The park is _____ the hospital. (near / in front of)
items.answer: near

items.q: The post office is _____ the bookstore. (behind / in front of)
items.answer: in front of

blocks.instruction: Do as directed. Use will to talk about the future.

items.q: Rewrite each sentence with will. (a) Meena waters the plants. (b) Asha stands behind Ravi and cheers loudly.
items.answer: (a) Meena will water the plants. (1) (b) Asha will stand behind Ravi and cheer loudly. (1) Also accept: Asha will stand behind Ravi and will cheer loudly.

answerPoints.point: Asha will stand behind Ravi and (will) cheer loudly

items.chapterSource: Let us Write (note: will for the future)

items.q: Complete each sentence with will and the word from the brackets. (a) Tomorrow, Kabir _____ the plants near the school. (water) (b) Next week, our class _____ the hospital. (visit)
items.chapterSource: Let us Write (note: will for the future)

items.q: Rearrange the words to make a sentence. Begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop. (a) will / near / stop / bus / hospital / the / the (b) will / behind / children / school / play / the / the
items.answer: (a) The bus will stop near the hospital. (1) (b) The children will play behind the school. (1) Also accept: Near the hospital, the bus will stop. / Behind the school, the children will play.

answerPoints.point: The bus will stop near the hospital.
The children will play behind the school.

items.chapterSource: Let us Learn B; Let us Write (will)

items.q: Look again at the map for Q.8. (a) Write one true sentence about the map, using behind. (b) Write one true sentence about the map, using between. (c) Write one sentence about what you will do tomorrow. (d) Write one sentence about what you will do next week. Use will in (c) and (d).
items.answer: (a) One of: The hospital is behind the bank. / The bookstore is behind the post office. / The park is behind the school. (1) (b) One of: The bank is between the post office and the school. / The hospital is between the bookstore and the park. (1) (c) and (d) Any sensible sentence with will, for example: I will play cricket tomorrow. / I will visit my aunt next week. (1 each)

answerPoints.point: (d) sentence with will about next week

items.markingGuide: Check (a) and (b) against the map: the sentence must be true and use the word correctly. For (c) and (d) the sentence must use will and a plain action word. One mark each, 4 in all. Do not deduct for spelling in this item.
items.skill: read the map and write; write what you will do next
items.chapterSource: Let us Learn B (map); Let us Write (will)

items.q: Each sentence has one mistake. Write each sentence correctly. For (c) and (d), use the map for Q.8. (a) Tomorrow, Asha will plays cricket. (b) Next week, we will visiting the hospital. (c) The school is behind the park. (d) The park is between the hospital.
items.answer: (a) Tomorrow, Asha will play cricket. (1) (b) Next week, we will visit the hospital. (1) (c) The school is in front of the park. (1) (Also accept: The park is behind the school.) (d) The park is near the hospital. (1) (Accept any true, correct sentence that keeps the park and the hospital.)

answerPoints.point: (c) in front of the park (or the park is behind the school)

items.chapterSource: Let us Learn B (map); Let us Write (will)

blocks.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

items.q: Match the words with their meanings.
items.answer: unity – the feeling of being together as one group; bond – a close link that ties people together; trust – the belief that someone is honest and will not let you down; cheer – to shout happily to support someone; share – to give a part of what you have to someone else

pairs.right: the feeling of being together as one group
a close link that ties people together
the belief that someone is honest and will not let you down
to shout happily to support someone
to give a part of what you have to someone else

items.chapterSource: poem l.1-10 and Let us Speak (unity)

blocks.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the words from the box. Use each word once. Box: choir, swarm, grove, bunch.

items.q: A _____ of bees buzzed around the hive.
items.answer: swarm

items.q: A _____ of boys sang at the school function.
items.answer: choir

items.q: A _____ of mango trees grew near the pond.
items.answer: grove

items.q: Meera gave her teacher a _____ of flowers.
items.answer: bunch
items.chapterSource: Let us Learn A (bunch / bouquet of flowers)

items.q: Write the word from the chapter for each meaning. (a) the sweet liquid inside a flower that bees collect (b) a large group of ants that live and work together
items.answer: (a) nectar (1) (b) colony (1)

items.q: Write two sentences of your own. Use “a herd of” in one sentence and “a pack of” in the other.
items.answer: For example: A herd of cows crossed the road. (1) A pack of wolves ran through the forest. (1)

answerPoints.point: sentence with a herd of and a sensible noun
sentence with a pack of and a sensible noun

items.markingGuide: One mark for each sentence that uses the group word with a sensible noun (herd: cows, sheep, deer, elephants; pack: wolves, dogs, cards). Two — 2; one — 1. Do not deduct for spelling in this item.

items.q: Circle the correct spelling. (the customs that families follow for many years)
items.answer: traditions

items.q: Circle the correct spelling. (to talk or share news with others)
items.answer: communicate

blocks.instruction: Rearrange the jumbled letters to make meaningful words.

items.q: Put the letters in order to write three words from this chapter. (a) ILGSNSA = _____ (b) VOEORCME = _____ (c) AFTESSVIL = _____
items.chapterSource: Know You Do (signals); poem l.4 (overcome); Let us Speak (festivals)
